evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run remedial math classes in 60 government upper-primary schools in Bihar for Grade 6 and 7 students who scored below the Grade 4 level on our baseline. Behavior: those students attend the daily remedial hour for the full 10-week block. We interviewed 40 of them: 26 said things like 'maths is for the sharp ones, I am not sharp'. Cost and distance are not the issue. The remedial teachers are our own trained instructors; they give each student a worked problem back every day, and there is a level test at week 5 and week 10. We don't know what friends say about attending. Delivery: one 60-minute session in Hindi in the first week of the block, on paper, run by our instructors; many students read slowly. We can measure the week-10 level test and daily attendance, and we can hold 30 schools back as a comparison. Adapt the lesson for us.
evals.expected_output: An adapted growth-mindset lesson in the output template, with the check of the school filled in from the facts given.
assertions: Records the daily worked problem and the two level tests as what the school offers, and marks what peers say as not verified.
The lesson has the three claims, each with an example that is local and not from the United States, and no wording tells students to work or try harder.
Includes the task of writing advice to a younger student, with a spoken version for slow readers.
Names the week-10 level test or attendance as the outcome, and a belief item only as a check that the lesson was received.
States that the pooled effect is near zero or that the Argentina trial found none, and promises no effect size.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our students think they are bad at math. Write us a growth mindset lesson.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the students' own words, what the school offers after a poor result, and who will receive the lesson, and writes nothing else.
assertions: Asks for evidence, in students' own words, that they read a poor result as proof of fixed ability.
Asks what the school offers after a poor result: feedback, a second attempt, or what teachers and peers say.
Asks who receives the lesson or how it will be delivered.
Writes no lesson text.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: The Ministry of Education wants to drop the planned remedial reading program in 1,800 primary schools in Malawi because it costs too much, and put a one-hour growth-mindset session in its place for all Standard 5 pupils next term. We interviewed 30 pupils: 17 said things like 'reading is for the clever ones'. Classes have about 90 pupils, teachers do not return written work, and there is one end-of-year exam with no second sitting. They want the session in Chichewa, run by class teachers, ready in four weeks. Please produce it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the school does not give pupils a way to improve, writes no lesson for delivery, and tells the user to bring in an evaluator before the national decision.
assertions: Says the setting does not deliver, citing the unreturned work or the single exam with no second sitting.
Says what would have to change first.
Says the session cannot replace the remedial reading program.
Tells the user to consult an education evaluator or a psychologist with experience of school interventions.
States the record for growth-mindset lessons and promises no effect size.
Does not write a lesson for delivery.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: First-year students from rural districts at our polytechnic in Kumasi drop out in the first term. In interviews they say 'people from the villages don't last here' and 'the city students already know each other'. The dean wants a growth mindset session at orientation. Can you adapt one?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the students' words are about belonging, not ability, and points to the skill for belonging stories.
assertions: Says the quotes are about whether people like them belong, not about ability.
Names draft-belonging-story or identify-wise-intervention-target.
Writes no lesson text.
